cases.input_text: Customer expressions of dissatisfaction involving AI chatbots or automated credit scoring must be broadly recognized as complaints under ASIC RG 271.
expected_atomic_requirements: Broadly recognize customer dissatisfaction with AI as complaints under ASIC RG 271

cases.input_text: All customer complaints regarding AI decisions must be recorded in the centralized dispute register within 1 business day.
expected_atomic_requirements: Record AI complaints in centralized register within 1 business day

cases.input_text: The bank must provide a comprehensive written IDR response to consumer credit complaints involving automated models within a maximum of 30 calendar days.
expected_atomic_requirements: Provide written IDR response to credit complaints within 30 calendar days
cases.notes: ASIC RG 271 para 56 30-day statutory response horizon.

cases.input_text: Written IDR responses must inform complainants of their right to escalate unresolved AI disputes to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA).
expected_atomic_requirements: Inform complainants in IDR responses of right to escalate to AFCA

cases.input_text: Customer dispute management systems must provide an immediate option to transfer from automated chatbot handling to a human dispute resolution specialist.
expected_atomic_requirements: Provide immediate option to transfer from chatbot to human dispute specialist

cases.input_text: Complaint data from automated decision systems must be analyzed monthly to identify recurring systemic issues and model logic defects.
expected_atomic_requirements: Monthly analysis of complaint data to identify systemic issues and model defects

cases.input_text: A systemic issue threshold is triggered when more than 5 customer complaints identify the identical algorithmic credit refusal rationale in a calendar month.
expected_atomic_requirements: Trigger systemic issue when more than 5 complaints identify identical refusal rationale

cases.input_text: When a systemic algorithmic error is confirmed, the bank must proactively identify, communicate with, and remediate all affected customers.
expected_atomic_requirements: Proactively identify and remediate all affected customers for confirmed systemic errors

cases.input_text: Systemic AI dispute root causes must be formally reported to the Board Audit & Risk Committee on a quarterly basis under ASIC RG 271.
expected_atomic_requirements: Quarterly reporting of systemic AI dispute root causes to Board Audit & Risk Committee
cases.notes: Holdout: Board escalation of systemic complaints.

cases.input_text: Does the customer intake flow provide a clear, free-of-charge mechanism for individuals to dispute an adverse AI outcome with a human operator?
expected_atomic_requirements: Inquire whether intake flow provides clear, free mechanism to dispute AI outcome with human

cases.input_text: Customer service staff shall not refuse to register an oral expression of dissatisfaction simply because the customer cannot identify the specific AI algorithm involved.
expected_atomic_requirements: Prohibit refusing oral complaints because customer cannot identify specific algorithm

cases.input_text: Remediation payments for algorithmic overcharging errors must be calculated and disbursed to impacted cardholders within 60 days of systemic confirmation.
expected_atomic_requirements: Disburse remediation payments for algorithmic overcharging within 60 days of confirmation

cases.input_text: Automated lending platforms must capture the consumer's specific requirements and loan objectives prior to issuing an automated preliminary credit assessment.
expected_atomic_requirements: Capture consumer requirements and objectives prior to preliminary credit assessment

cases.input_text: Consumer financial situations, income, and non-discretionary expenses must be verified from reliable third-party evidence (such as bank transaction feeds) rather than self-declared claims.
expected_atomic_requirements: Verify consumer financial situation and expenses from reliable third-party feeds

cases.input_text: The automated decision engine must enforce an unsuitability filter that rejects loan contracts if the consumer will be unable to meet financial obligations without substantial hardship.
expected_atomic_requirements: Enforce unsuitability filter rejecting loans causing substantial financial hardship

cases.input_text: A written copy of the credit unsuitability assessment must be generated and stored, retrievable for consumer provision within 7 business days of request.
expected_atomic_requirements: Generate and store written credit unsuitability assessment retrievable within 7 business days
cases.notes: NCCP Act s 132 written assessment retrieval.

cases.input_text: Australian Credit Licence (ACL) holders deploying automated credit tools must ensure services are provided efficiently, honestly, and fairly under Section 47.
expected_atomic_requirements: Ensure automated credit tools operate efficiently, honestly and fairly under s 47
cases.notes: NCCP Act s 47 general licensee conduct.

cases.input_text: Credit compliance teams must monitor automated loan approvals continuously to identify statutory breaches of responsible lending provisions.
expected_atomic_requirements: Continuously monitor automated loan approvals for responsible lending breaches

cases.input_text: Does the automated credit scoring pipeline capture and independently verify customer expenses against primary banking statements before issuing loan approval?
expected_atomic_requirements: Inquire whether automated pipeline captures and verifies expenses against bank statements
cases.notes: Holdout: Responsible lending verification questionnaire check.

cases.input_text: Credit decisioning models shall not approve personal loans where applicant living expenses are estimated solely using benchmark poverty indexes without actual verification.
expected_atomic_requirements: Prohibit loan approvals where living expenses are estimated solely from poverty benchmarks
cases.notes: Holdout: Responsible lending benchmark prohibition (HEM benchmark case).

cases.input_text: The bank must confirm whether the AI system is placed on the market or used in the European Union, establishing territorial nexus under Article 2 of the EU AI Act.
expected_atomic_requirements: Confirm whether AI system establishes EU territorial nexus under Article 2
cases.notes: EU AI Act Article 2 territorial scope.

cases.input_text: AI systems utilized to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score are classified as High-Risk AI Systems under Annex III(5)(b).
expected_atomic_requirements: Classify creditworthiness evaluation AI as High-Risk under Annex III(5)(b)

cases.input_text: Deployers of High-Risk credit evaluation AI systems must retain system logs generated by the AI system for at least 6 months under Article 26.
expected_atomic_requirements: Retain system logs for High-Risk credit AI for at least 6 months under Article 26
cases.notes: EU AI Act Article 26 deployer log retention.

cases.input_text: AI systems used strictly for the purpose of detecting financial fraud are exempt from High-Risk classification under Annex III(5)(b).
expected_atomic_requirements: Exempt dedicated financial fraud detection systems from High-Risk classification
cases.notes: EU AI Act fraud detection exception.

cases.input_text: Prior to deploying high-risk credit scoring AI in the EU, the deployer must complete a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) under Article 27.
expected_atomic_requirements: Complete Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) under Article 27 prior to deployment
cases.notes: EU AI Act Article 27 FRIA requirement.

cases.input_text: AI systems that deploy subliminal techniques or exploit vulnerabilities of specific demographic groups to materially distort behavior are strictly prohibited under Article 5.
expected_atomic_requirements: Prohibit AI systems deploying subliminal techniques or exploiting vulnerabilities under Article 5
cases.notes: Holdout: EU AI Act Article 5 prohibited practice.

cases.input_text: A domestic Australian credit union offering home loans strictly to residents of New South Wales without any EU operations or marketing has zero EU AI Act compliance obligations.
expected_atomic_requirements: Confirm domestic Australian credit union without EU operations is exempt from EU AI Act
cases.notes: Holdout test: Statutory non-applicability rule verification. Zero active EU high-risk compliance obligations.

cases.input_text: All staff operating high-risk banking AI tools must have documented evidence of AI literacy training under Article 4 of the EU AI Act.
expected_atomic_requirements: Document evidence of AI literacy training for staff operating high-risk AI tools
cases.notes: Holdout: EU AI Act Article 4 staff literacy.
